stem: An agriculture study measures the yield per hectare (tonnes) for a sample of 30 farms. The sample mean is 7.9 tonnes with a sample standard deviation of 1.4 tonnes. However, 2 of the 30 observations appear to be outliers (values more than 2.5 standard deviations from the mean). If these outliers are removed, the remaining 28 observations have a mean of 7.5 tonnes and standard deviation of 1.0 tonnes. Estimate the true population mean and provide a 95% confidence interval that accounts for the uncertainty about whether outliers should be included.

ground_truth.answer: With all data: mean = 7.9, 95% CI = [7.4, 8.4]. Without outliers: mean = 7.5, 95% CI = [7.1, 7.9]. Combined interval accounting for analytic uncertainty: [7.1, 8.4]. Point estimate: 7.7 tonnes.

solution_steps: The outlier treatment choice creates structural uncertainty. Combined interval: [7.1, 8.4].
common_failure_modes: Using only the full sample without considering outlier impact
Removing outliers without reporting both analyses
Not recognizing that the choice of analysis method is itself a source of uncertainty
